study_type: Five fresh independent simulated beginners, not a human user study
agent_context: Fresh fork_turns=none tasks; no baseline results, source code or peer sessions provided
task: Compose a 30-second piece using audio plus MIDI through a VST instrument, save the project and export WAV and MIDI using only a mouse. Give the piece a chosen name if possible.
comparison_note: Core task matches baseline. Personalized naming is explicitly encouraged in round 2 to exercise the resolved mouse-only naming gap. Elapsed session time includes screenshots and reporting pauses and is not a human performance benchmark.
inputs: Only screenshots plus logged click, double-click, drag, scroll and pointer move. No keyboard input, project injection or source inspection during attempt.
reset: Five new native windows, fresh caches and working directories, no projects from round1. Configuration is fresh except a documented1024-frame lab output buffer. Unchanged stock starter audio and same native Rill Lab Sine VST3.
rating_scale: 1–5; higher means more of named quality. Higher confusion is worse.
audio: Per-session timer-paced PulseAudio virtual sink via ALSA bridge at48kHz. Lab configuration: Rill requested1024 output frames and PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=60. No physical hardware or listening claims; this is not a latency benchmark.
validation: Independent read-only verification of saved project ZIP, embedded audio, native VST identity, MIDI events and all exported WAV samples.
reporting: Observable action/reaction summaries, screenshots and timestamped mouse logs, not private reasoning transcripts.
frozen_build: Native executable and adjacent plugin helper snapshotted only after regression verification; source file hashes and binary SHA-256 recorded.
audio_setup_correction: A blocking-writer test did not predict CPAL callback bursts. A60ms Pulse override with the256-frame app buffer underrun the queue; ordinary negotiation also produced ALSA startup errors. Actual-app checks accepted1024 requested frames plus60ms Pulse buffering: ~48,068 frames/s, zero device/render errors, no additional queue underruns after one startup underrun. No production queue tuning.
